key_pathways: Hepatic metabolism via sulfation and glucuronidation

avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May induce hepatic metabolism and reduce fulvestrant exposure; potential loss of efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; consider alternative mood support if needed

avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Vitamin E (>400 IU daily)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May potentiate anticoagulant effects and increase bleeding risk in patients on concurrent anticoagulants
avoid_supplements.action: Limit vitamin E supplementation; monitor for signs of bleeding

caution_supplements.name: Ginseng
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have estrogenic properties; theoretical potential to antagonize fulvestrant effects
caution_supplements.action: Monitor clinical response; discuss use with oncology team

caution_supplements.name: Red Clover
caution_supplements.mechanism: Contains isoflavones with estrogenic activity; may theoretically reduce fulvestrant efficacy
caution_supplements.action: Avoid or use with caution; inform healthcare provider of use

caution_foods.name: Grapefruit and grapefruit juice
caution_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibitor; fulvestrant not primarily CYP3A4-dependent but excessive consumption may alter hepatic metabolism
caution_foods.action: Limit grapefruit consumption; no strict avoidance required but moderate intake recommended

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May affect absorption and distribution of intramuscular fulvestrant; does not significantly impact efficacy but consistency advised
caution_foods.action: Maintain consistent dietary fat intake; not a critical concern for this IM formulation

monitoring_notes: Fulvestrant is minimally metabolized by CYP450 enzymes, reducing drug-drug and supplement-drug interactions. Primary monitoring should focus on estrogenic supplements that may antagonize SERD activity and anticoagulant interactions, particularly in patients on concurrent anticoagulation therapy.
